transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jeremy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I appreciate your — your question, and thank you for being here this evening and to all of those from Nassau County that have come, thank you for your time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you to Hofstra University and to Candy Crowley for organizing and leading this — this event.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, also for being part of this — this debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Your question — your question is one that’s being asked by college kids all over this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was in Pennsylvania with someone who had just graduated — this was in Philadelphia — and she said, “I’ve got my degree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I can’t find a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got three part- time jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re just barely enough to pay for my food and pay for an apartment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I can’t begin to pay back my student loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” So what we have to do is two things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to make sure that we make it easier for kids to afford college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And also make sure that when they get out of college, there’s a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When I was governor of Massachusetts, to get a high school degree, you had to pass an exam.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If you graduated in the top quarter of your airlines, we gave you a John and Abigail Adams scholarship, four years tuition free in the college of your choice in Massachusetts, it’s a public institution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure we keep our Pell grant program growing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re also going to have our loan program, so that people are able to afford school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the key thing is to make sure you can get a job when you get out of school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And what’s happened over the last four years has been very, very hard for America’s young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want you to be able to get a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know what it takes to get this economy going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: With half of college kids graduating this year without a college — excuse me, without a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And without a college level job, that’s just unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And likewise you’ve got more and more debt on your back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So more debt and less jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to change that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know what it takes to create good jobs again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know what it takes to make sure that you have the kind of opportunity you deserve.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And kids across this country are going to recognize, we’re bringing back an economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not going to be like the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The middle-class has been crushed over the last four years, and jobs have been too scarce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know what it takes to bring them back, and I’m going to do that, and make sure that when you graduate — when do you graduate?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When you come out in 2014, I presume I’m going to be president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to make sure you get a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thanks Jeremy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, you bet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Jeremy, first of all, your future is bright.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the fact that you’re making an investment in higher education is critical.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not just to you, but to the entire nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, the most important thing we can do is to make sure that we are creating jobs in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But not just jobs, good paying jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ones that can support a family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I want to do, is build on the five million jobs that we’ve created over the last 30 months in the private sector alone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And there are a bunch of things we can do to make sure your future is bright.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one, I want to build manufacturing jobs in this country again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now when Governor Romney said we should let Detroit go bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said we’re going to bet on American workers and the American auto industry and it’s come surging back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to do that in industries, not just in Detroit, but all across the country and that means we change our tax code so we’re giving incentives to companies that are investing here in the United States and creating jobs here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It also means we’re helping them and small businesses to export all around the world to new markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we’ve got to make sure that we have the best education system in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the fact that you’re going to college is great, but I want everybody to get a great education and we’ve worked hard to make sure that student loans are available for folks like you, but I also want to make sure that community colleges are offering slots for workers to get retrained for the jobs that are out there right now and the jobs of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number three, we’ve got to control our own energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, not only oil and natural gas, which we’ve been investing in; but also, we’ve got to make sure we’re building the energy source of the future, not just thinking about next year, but ten years from now, 20 years from now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we’ve invested in solar and wind and biofuels, energy efficient cars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to reduce our deficit, but we’ve got to do it in a balanced way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Asking the wealthy to pay a little bit more along with cuts so that we can invest in education like yours.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And let’s take the money that we’ve been spending on war over the last decade to rebuild America, roads, bridges schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We do those things, not only is your future going to be bright but America’s future is going to bright as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well what you’re seeing in this country is 23 million people struggling to find a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And a lot of them, as you say, Candy, have been out of work for a long, long, long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s policies have been exercised over the last four years and they haven’t put Americans back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have fewer people working today than we had when the president took office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If the — the unemployment rate was 7.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 8 percent when he took office, it’s 7.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 8 percent now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But if you calculated that unemployment rate, taking back the people who dropped out of the workforce, it would be 10.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 7 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have not made the progress we need to make to put people back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I put out a five-point plan that gets America 12 million new jobs in four years and rising take-home pay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to help Jeremy get a job when he comes out of school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to help people across the country that are unemployed right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And one thing that the president said, which I want to make sure that we understand, he said that I said we should take Detroit bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that’s right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My plan was to have the company go through bankruptcy like 7-Eleven did and Macy’s and Condell Airlines and come out stronger.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I know he keeps saying, you want to take Detroit bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, the president took Detroit bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You took General Motors bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You took Chrysler bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So when you say that I wanted to take the auto industry bankrupt, you actually did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s important to know that that was a process that was necessary to get those companies back on their feet, so they could start hiring more people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That was precisely what I recommended and ultimately what happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That — that Detroit — that Detroit answer…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … that Detroit answer…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … and the rest of the answer, way off the mark.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The most important thing we can do is to make sure we control our own energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So here’s what I’ve done since I’ve been president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have increased oil production to the highest levels in 16 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Natural gas production is the highest it’s been in decades.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We have seen increases in coal production and coal employment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what I’ve also said is we can’t just produce traditional source of energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve also got to look to the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we doubled fuel efficiency standards on cars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That means that in the middle of the next decade, any car you buy, you’re going to end up going twice as far on a gallon of gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we doubled clean — clean energy production like wind and solar and biofuels.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And all these things have contributed to us lowering our oil imports to the lowest levels in 16 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, I want to build on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that means, yes, we still continue to open up new areas for drilling.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We continue to make it a priority for us to go after natural gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got potentially 600,000 jobs and 100 years worth of energy right beneath our feet with natural gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we can do it in an environmentally sound way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve also got to continue to figure out how we have efficiency energy, because ultimately that’s how we’re going to reduce demand and that’s what’s going to keep gas prices lower.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney will say he’s got an all-of-the-above plan, but basically his plan is to let the oil companies write the energy policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So he’s got the oil and gas part, but he doesn’t have the clean energy part.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we are only thinking about tomorrow or the next day and not thinking about 10 years from now, we’re not going to control our own economic future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because China, Germany, they’re making these investments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’m not going to cede those jobs of the future to those countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I expect those new energy sources to be built right here in the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to help Jeremy get a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s also going to make sure that you’re not paying as much for gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, let’s look at the president’s policies, all right, as opposed to the rhetoric, because we’ve had four years of policies being played out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the president’s right in terms of the additional oil production, but none of it came on federal land.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, oil production is down 14 percent this year on federal land, and gas production was down 9 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Why?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because the president cut in half the number of licenses and permits for drilling on federal lands, and in federal waters.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So where’d the increase come from?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well a lot of it came from the Bakken Range in North Dakota.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What was his participation there?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The administration brought a criminal action against the people drilling up there for oil, this massive new resource we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And what was the cost?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 20 or 25 birds were killed and brought out a migratory bird act to go after them on a criminal basis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, I want to make sure we use our oil, our coal, our gas, our nuclear, our renewables.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I believe very much in our renewable capabilities; ethanol, wind, solar will be an important part of our energy mix.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But what we don’t need is to have the president keeping us from taking advantage of oil, coal and gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This has not been Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Oil, or Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Gas, or Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Coal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Talk to the people that are working in those industries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was in coal country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: People grabbed my arms and said, “Please save my job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” The head of the EPA said, “You can’t build a coal plant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ll virtually — it’s virtually impossible given our regulations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” When the president ran for office, he said if you build a coal plant, you can go ahead, but you’ll go bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the right course for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s take advantage of the energy resources we have, as well as the energy sources for the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And if we do that, if we do what I’m planning on doing, which is getting us energy independent, North America energy independence within eight years, you’re going to see manufacturing jobs come back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because our energy is low cost, that are already beginning to come back because of our abundant energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get America and North America energy independent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll do it by more drilling, more permits and licenses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to bring that pipeline in from Canada.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How in the world the president said no to that pipeline?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will never know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is about bringing good jobs back for the middle class of America, and that’s what I’m going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: CROWLEY: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, let me just see if I can move you to the gist of this question, which is, are we looking at the new normal?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I can tell you that tomorrow morning, a lot of people in Hempstead will wake up and fill up and they will find that the price of gas is over $4 a gallon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Is it within the purview of the government to bring those prices down, or are we looking at the new normal?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Candy, there’s no doubt that world demand’s gone up, but our production is going up, and we’re using oil more efficiently.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And very little of what Governor Romney just said is true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve opened up public lands.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re actually drilling more on public lands than in the previous administration and my — the previous president was an oil man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And natural gas isn’t just appearing magically.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re encouraging it and working with the industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when I hear Governor Romney say he’s a big coal guy, I mean, keep in mind, when — Governor, when you were governor of Massachusetts, you stood in front of a coal plant and pointed at it and said, “This plant kills,” and took great pride in shutting it down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And now suddenly you’re a big champion of coal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what I’ve tried to do is be consistent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: With respect to something like coal, we made the largest investment in clean coal technology, to make sure that even as we’re producing more coal, we’re producing it cleaner and smarter.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Same thing with oil, same thing with natural gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the proof is our oil imports are down to the lowest levels in 20 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Oil production is up, natural gas production is up, and, most importantly, we’re also starting to build cars that are more efficient.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s creating jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That means those cars can be exported, ’cause that’s the demand around the world, and it also means that it’ll save money in your pocketbook.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the strategy you need, an all-of-the-above strategy, and that’s what we’re going to do in the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But that’s not what you’ve done in the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In the last four years, you cut permits and licenses on federal land and federal waters in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not true, Governor Romney.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So how much did you cut ?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How much did you cut them by, then?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor, we have actually produced more oil —

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No, no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How much did you cut licenses and permits on federal land and federal waters?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney, here’s what we did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There were a whole bunch of oil companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No, no, I had a question and the question was how much did you cut them by?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You want me to answer a question —

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How much did you cut them by?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m happy to answer the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: All right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And it is —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Here’s what happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You had a whole bunch of oil companies who had leases on public lands that they weren’t using.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what we said was you can’t just sit on this for 10, 20, 30 years, decide when you want to drill, when you want to produce, when it’s most profitable for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These are public lands.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So if you want to drill on public lands, you use it or you lose it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: OK, —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so what we did was take away those leases.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are now reletting them so that we can actually make a profit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And production on private — on government land —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Production is up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: — is down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, it isn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Production on government land of oil is down 14 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor —

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And production on gas —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s just not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s absolutely true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, there’s no question but the people recognize that we have not produced more on federal lands and in federal waters.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And coal, coal production is not up; coal jobs are not up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was just at a coal facility, where some 1,200 people lost their jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The right course for America is to have a true all-of-the-above policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think anyone really believes that you’re a person who’s going to be pushing for oil and gas and coal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ll get your chance in a moment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m still speaking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well —

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the answer is I don’t believe people think that’s the case —

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That wasn’t the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That was a statement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think the American people believe that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will fight for oil, coal and natural gas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the proof, the proof of whether a strategy is working or not is what the price is that you’re paying at the pump.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If you’re paying less than you paid a year or two ago, why, then, the strategy is working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But you’re paying more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When the president took office, the price of gasoline here in Nassau County was about $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 86 a gallon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And let me tell you, you’re absolutely right about part of that, which is I want to bring the rates down, I want to simplify the tax code, and I want to get middle- income taxpayers to have lower taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the reason I want middle-income taxpayers to have lower taxes is because middle-income taxpayers have been buried over the past four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ve seen, as middle-income people in this country, incomes go down $4,300 a family, even as gasoline prices have gone up $2,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Health insurance premiums, up $2,500.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Food prices up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Utility prices up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The middle-income families in America have been crushed over the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I want to get some relief to middle-income families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s part — that’s part one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, how about deductions?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ‘Cause I’m going to bring rates down across the board for everybody, but I’m going to limit deductions and exemptions and credits, particularly for people at the high end, because I am not going to have people at the high end pay less than they’re paying now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The top 5 percent of taxpayers will continue to pay 60 percent of the income tax the nation collects.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So that’ll stay the same.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Middle-income people are going to get a tax break.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so, in terms of bringing down deductions, one way of doing that would be say everybody gets — I’ll pick a number — $25,000 of deductions and credits, and you can decide which ones to use.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Your home mortgage interest deduction, charity, child tax credit, and so forth, you can use those as part of filling that bucket, if you will, of deductions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But your rate comes down and the burden also comes down on you for one more reason, and that is every middle-income taxpayer no longer will pay any tax on interest, dividends or capital gains.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No tax on your savings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That makes life a lot easier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If you’re getting interest from a bank, if you’re getting a statement from a mutual fund or any other kind of investment you have, you don’t have to worry about filing taxes on that, because there’ll be no taxes for anybody making $200,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 00 per year and less, on your interest, dividends and capital gains.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Why am I lowering taxes on the middle-class?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because under the last four years, they’ve been buried.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I want to help people in the middle-class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I will not — I will not under any circumstances, reduce the share that’s being paid by the highest income taxpayers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I will not, under any circumstances increase taxes on the middle-class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s spending, the president’s borrowing will cost this nation to have to raise taxes on the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Not just at the high end.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A recent study has shown the people in the middle-class will see $4,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will not let that happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My philosophy on taxes has been simple.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that is, I want to give middle-class families and folks who are striving to get into the middle-class some relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because they have been hit hard over the last decade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Over the last 15, over the last 20 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So four years ago I stood on a stage just like this one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Actually it was a town hall, and I said I would cut taxes for middle- class families, and that’s what I’ve done, by $3,600.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said I would cut taxes for small businesses, who are the drivers and engines of growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve cut them 18 times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I want to continue those tax cuts for middle-class families, and for small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what I’ve also said is, if we’re serious about reducing the deficit, if this is genuinely a moral obligation to the next generation, then in addition to some tough spending cuts, we’ve also got to make sure that the wealthy do a little bit more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what I’ve said is, your first $250,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: 00 worth of income, no change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that means 98 percent of American families, 97 percent of small businesses, they will not see a tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m ready to sign that bill right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The only reason it’s not happening is because Governor Romney’s allies in Congress have held the 98 percent hostage because they want tax breaks for the top 2 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what I’ve also says is for above $250,000, we can go back to the tax rates we had when Bill Clinton was president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We created 23 million new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s part of what took us from deficits to surplus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It will be good for our economy and it will be good for job creation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney has a different philosophy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He was on 60 Minutes just two weeks ago and he was asked: Is it fair for somebody like you, making $20 million a year, to pay a lower tax rate than a nurse or a bus driver, somebody making $50,000 year?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And he said, “Yes, I think that’s fair.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” Not only that, he said, “I think that’s what grows the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” Well, I fundamentally disagree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think what grows the economy is when you get that tax credit that we put in place for your kids going to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that grows the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think what grows the economy is when we make sure small businesses are getting a tax credit for hiring veterans who fought for our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That grows our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we just have a different theory.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when Governor Romney stands here, after a year of campaigning, when during a Republican primary he stood on stage and said “I’m going to give tax cuts” — he didn’t say tax rate cuts, he said “tax cuts to everybody,” including the top 1 percent, you should believe him because that’s been his history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s exactly the kind of top-down economics that is not going to work if we want a strong middle class and an economy that’s striving for everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, it’s not settled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, the cost of lowering rates for everybody across the board, 20 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Along with what he also wants to do in terms of eliminating the estate tax, along what he wants to do in terms of corporates, changes in the tax code, it costs about $5 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney then also wants to spend $2 trillion on additional military programs even though the military’s not asking for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s $7 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He also wants to continue the Bush tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s another trillion dollars — that’s $8 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, what he says is he’s going to make sure that this doesn’t add to the deficit and he’s going to cut middleclass taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when he’s asked, how are you going to do it, which deductions, which loopholes are you going to close?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He can’t tell you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The — the fact that he only has to pay 14 percent on his taxes when a lot of you are paying much higher.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He’s already taken that off the board, capital gains are going to continue to be at a low rate so we — we’re not going to get money that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We haven’t heard from the governor any specifics beyond Big Bird and eliminating funding for Planned Parenthood in terms of how he pays for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney was a very successful investor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If somebody came to you, Governor, with a plan that said, here, I want to spend $7 or $8 trillion, and then we’re going to pay for it, but we can’t tell you until maybe after the election how we’re going to do it, you wouldn’t take such a sketchy deal and neither should you, the American people, because the math doesn’t add up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And — and what’s at stake here is one of two things, either Candy — this blows up the deficit because keep in mind, this is just to pay for the additional spending that he’s talking about, $7 trillion – $8 trillion before we even get to the deficit we already have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Or, alternatively, it’s got to be paid for, not only by closing deductions for wealthy individuals, that — that will pay for about 4 percent reduction in tax rates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to be paying for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to lose some deductions, and you can’t buy the sales pitch.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nobody who’s looked at it that’s serious, actually believes it adds up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well of course they add up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I was — I was someone who ran businesses for 25 years, and balanced the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I ran the Olympics and balanced the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I ran the — the state of Massachusetts as a governor, to the extent any governor does, and balanced the budget all four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When we’re talking about math that doesn’t add up, how about $4 trillion of deficits over the last four years, $5 trillion?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s math that doesn’t add up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have — we have a president talking about someone’s plan in a way that’s completely foreign to what my real plan is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then we have his own record, which is we have four consecutive years where he said when he was running for office, he would cut the deficit in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Instead he’s doubled it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve gone from $10 trillion of national debt, to $16 trillion of national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If the president were reelected, we’d go to almost $20 trillion of national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This puts us on a road to Greece.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know what it takes to balance budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve done it my entire life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So for instance when he says, “Yours is a $5 trillion cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” Well, no it’s not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because I’m offsetting some of the reductions with holding down some of the deductions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I just described — I just described to you, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President — I just described to you precisely how I’d do it which is with a single number that people can put — and they can put they’re — they’re deductions and credits…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Looking forward to it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it’s Katherine Fenton, who has a question for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Katherine, that’s a great question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, I was raised by a single mom who had to put herself through school while looking after two kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And she worked hard every day and made a lot of sacrifices to make sure we got everything we needed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My grandmother, she started off as a secretary in a bank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: She never got a college education, even though she was smart as a whip.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And she worked her way up to become a vice president of a local bank, but she hit the glass ceiling.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: She trained people who would end up becoming her bosses during the course of her career.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: She didn’t complain.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what you did in that generation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is one of the reasons why one of the first — the first bill I signed was something called the Lily Ledbetter bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it’s named after this amazing woman who had been doing the same job as a man for years, found out that she was getting paid less, and the Supreme Court said that she couldn’t bring suit because she should have found about it earlier, whereas she had no way of finding out about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we fixed that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s an example of the kind of advocacy that we need, because women are increasingly the breadwinners in the family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is not just a women’s issue, this is a family issue, this is a middle-class issue, and that’s why we’ve got to fight for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It also means that we’ve got to make sure that young people like yourself are able to afford a college education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Earlier, Governor Romney talked about he wants to make Pell Grants and other education accessible for young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, the truth of the matter is, is that that’s exactly what we’ve done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve expanded Pell Grants for millions of people, including millions of young women, all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We did it by taking $60 billion that was going to banks and lenders as middlemen for the student loan program, and we said, let’s just cut out the middleman.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s give the money directly to students.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as a consequence, we’ve seen millions of young people be able to afford college, and that’s going to make sure that young women are going to be able to compete in that marketplace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve got to enforce the laws, which is what we are doing, and we’ve also got to make sure that in every walk of life we do not tolerate discrimination.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s been one of the hallmarks of my administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to continue to push on this issue for the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And important topic, and one which I learned a great deal about, particularly as I was serving as governor of my state, because I had the chance to pull together a cabinet and all the applicants seemed to be men.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I — and I went to my staff, and I said, “How come all the people for these jobs are — are all men.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” They said, “Well, these are the people that have the qualifications.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” And I said, “Well, gosh, can’t we — can’t we find some — some women that are also qualified?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and so we — we took a concerted effort to go out and find women who had backgrounds that could be qualified to become members of our cabinet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I went to a number of women’s groups and said, “Can you help us find folks,” and they brought us whole binders full of women.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was proud of the fact that after I staffed my Cabinet and my senior staff, that the University of New York in Albany did a survey of all 50 states, and concluded that mine had more women in senior leadership positions than any other state in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now one of the reasons I was able to get so many good women to be part of that team was because of our recruiting effort.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But number two, because I recognized that if you’re going to have women in the workforce that sometimes you need to be more flexible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My chief of staff, for instance, had two kids that were still in school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: She said, I can’t be here until 7 or 8 o’clock at night.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I need to be able to get home at 5 o’clock so I can be there for making dinner for my kids and being with them when they get home from school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So we said fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s have a flexible schedule so you can have hours that work for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to have employers in the new economy, in the economy I’m going to bring to play, that are going to be so anxious to get good workers they’re going to be anxious to hire women.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In the — in the last women have lost 580,000 jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s the net of what’s happened in the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re still down 580,000 jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I mentioned 31/2 million women, more now in poverty than four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What we can do to help young women and women of all ages is to have a strong economy, so strong that employers that are looking to find good employees and bringing them into their workforce and adapting to a flexible work schedule that gives women opportunities that they would otherwise not be able to afford.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is what I have done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s what I look forward to doing and I know what it takes to make an economy work, and I know what a working economy looks like.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And an economy with 7.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 8 percent unemployment is not a real strong economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: An economy that has 23 million people looking for work is not a strong economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: An economy with 50 percent of kids graduating from college that can’t finds a job, or a college level job, that’s not what we have to have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: CROWLEY: Governor?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to help women in America get good work by getting a stronger economy and by supporting women in the workforce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Katherine, I just want to point out that when Governor Romney’s campaign was asked about the Lilly Ledbetter bill, whether he supported it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He said, “I’ll get back to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And that’s not the kind of advocacy that women need in any economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, there are some other issues that have a bearing on how women succeed in the workplace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: For example, their healthcare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know a major difference in this campaign is that Governor Romney feels comfortable having politicians in Washington decide the health care choices that women are making.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In my health care bill, I said insurance companies need to provide contraceptive coverage to everybody who is insured.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because this is not just a — a health issue, it’s an economic issue for women.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It makes a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is money out of that family’s pocket.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney not only opposed it, he suggested that in fact employers should be able to make the decision as to whether or not a woman gets contraception through her insurance coverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the kind of advocacy that women need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When Governor Romney says that we should eliminate funding for Planned Parenthood, there are millions of women all across the country, who rely on Planned Parenthood for, not just contraceptive care, they rely on it for mammograms, for cervical cancer screenings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s a pocketbook issue for women and families all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it makes a difference in terms of how well and effectively women are able to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When we talk about child care, and the credits that we’re providing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That makes a difference in whether they can go out there and — and earn a living for their family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These are not just women’s issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These are family issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These are economic issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things that makes us grow as an economy is when everybody participates and women are getting the same fair deal as men are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve got two daughters and I want to make sure that they have the same opportunities that anybody’s sons have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s part of what I’m fighting for as president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I appreciate that question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I just want to make sure that, I think I was supposed to get that last answer, but I want to point out that that I don’t believe…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think so, Candy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … I don’t believe…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure our timekeepers are working here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The time — the time…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d just note that I don’t believe that bureaucrats in Washington should tell someone whether they can use contraceptives or not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t believe employers should tell someone whether they could have contraceptive care of not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Every woman in America should have access to contraceptives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and the — and the president’s statement of my policy is completely and totally wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me come back and — and answer your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President Bush and I are — are different people and these are different times and that’s why my five point plan is so different than what he would have done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I mean for instance, we can now, by virtue of new technology actually get all the energy we need in North America without having to go to the — the Arabs or the Venezuelans or anyone else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That wasn’t true in his time, that’s why my policy starts with a very robust policy to get all that energy in North America — become energy secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, trade — I’ll crack down on China, President Bush didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m also going to dramatically expand trade in Latin America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s been growing about 12 percent per year over a long period of time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to add more free trade agreements so we’ll have more trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number three, I’m going to get us to a balanced budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President Bush didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President Obama was right, he said that that was outrageous to have deficits as high as half a trillion dollars under the Bush years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He was right, but then he put in place deficits twice that size for every one of his four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And his forecast for the next four years is more deficits, almost that large.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So that’s the next area I’m different than President Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then let’s take the last one, championing small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Our party has been focused too long.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I came through small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I understand how hard it is to start a small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s why everything I’ll do is designed to help small businesses grow and add jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to keep their taxes down on small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want regulators to see their job as encouraging small enterprise, not crushing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the thing I find the most troubling about Obama Care, well it’s a long list, but one of the things I find most troubling is that when you go out and talk to small businesses and ask them what they think about it, they tell you it keeps them from hiring more people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My priority is jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know how to make that happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And President Bush has a very different path for a very different time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My path is designed in getting small businesses to grow and hire people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I think it’s important to tell you that we did come in during some tough times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We were losing 800,000 jobs a month when I started.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we had been digging our way out of policies that were misplaced and focused on the top doing very well and middle class folks not doing well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, we’ve seen 30 consecutive — 31 consecutive months of job growth; 5.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: 2 million new jobs created.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the plans that I talked about will create even more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when Governor Romney says that he has a very different economic plan, the centerpiece of his economic plan are tax cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what took us from surplus to deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When he talks about getting tough on China, keep in mind that Governor Romney invested in companies that were pioneers of outsourcing to China, and is currently investing in countries — in companies that are building surveillance equipment for China to spy on its own folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s — Governor, you’re the last person who’s going to get tough on China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what we’ve done when it comes to trade is not only sign three trade deals to open up new markets, but we’ve also set up a task force for trade that goes after anybody who is taking advantage of American workers or businesses and not creating a level playing field.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve brought twice as many cases against unfair trading practices than the previous administration and we’ve won every single one that’s been decided.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When I said that we had to make sure that China was not flooding our domestic market with cheap tires, Governor Romney said I was being protectionist; that it wouldn’t be helpful to American workers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, in fact we saved 1,000 jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the kind of tough trade actions that are required.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But the last point I want to make is this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, there are some things where Governor Romney is different from George Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: George Bush didn’t propose turning Medicare into a voucher.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: George Bush embraced comprehensive immigration reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He didn’t call for self-deportation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: George Bush never suggested that we eliminate funding for Planned Parenthood, so there are differences between Governor Romney and George Bush, but they’re not on economic policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In some ways, he’s gone to a more extreme place when it comes to social policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think that’s a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not how we’re going to move our economy forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, we’ve gone through a tough four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But four years ago, I told the American people and I told you I would cut taxes for middle class families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I told you I’d cut taxes for small businesses, and I have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said that I’d end the war in Iraq, and I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said we’d refocus attention on those who actually attacked us on 9/11, and we have gone after Al Qaeda’s leadership like never before and Osama bin Laden is dead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said that we would put in place health care reform to make sure that insurance companies can’t jerk you around and if you don’t have health insurance, that you’d have a chance to get affordable insurance, and I have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I committed that I would rein in the excesses of Wall Street, and we passed the toughest Wall Street reforms since the 1930s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve created five million jobs, and gone from 800 jobs a month being lost, and we are making progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We saved an auto industry that was on the brink of collapse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, does that mean you’re not struggling?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: A lot of us are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why the plan that I’ve put forward for manufacturing and education, and reducing our deficit in a sensible way, using the savings from ending wars, to rebuild America and putting people back to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Making sure that we are controlling our own energy, but not only the energy of today, but also the energy of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: All of those things will make a difference, so the point is the commitments I’ve made, I’ve kept.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And those that I haven’t been able to keep, it’s not for lack of trying and we’re going to get it done in a second term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, you should pay attention to this campaign, because Governor Romney has made some commitments as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I suspect he’ll keep those too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know when members of the Republican Congress say, “We’re going to sign a no tax pledge, so that we don’t ask a dime for millionaires and billionaires to reduce our deficit so we can still invest in education, and helping kids go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He said, “Me too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” When they said, “We’re going to cut Planned Parenthood funding.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” He said, “Me too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” When he said, “We’re going to repeal Obamacare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First thing I’m going to do,” despite the fact that it’s the same health care plan that he passed in Massachusetts and is working well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He said, “Me too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” That is not the kind of leadership that you need, but you should expect that those are promises he’s going to keep.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: …the choice in this election is going to be whose promises are going to be more likely to help you in your life?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Make sure your kids can go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Make sure that you are getting a good paying job, making sure that Medicare and Social Security…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: …will be there for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think you know better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think you know that these last four years haven’t been so good as the president just described and that you don’t feel like your confident that the next four years are going to be much better either.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I can tell you that if you were to elect President Obama, you know what you’re going to get.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to get a repeat of the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We just can’t afford four more years like the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said that by now we’d have unemployment at 5.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 4 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The difference between where it is and 5.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 4 percent is 9 million Americans without work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I wasn’t the one that said 5.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 4 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This was the president’s plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Didn’t get there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said he would have by now put forward a plan to reform Medicare and Social Security, because he pointed out they’re on the road to bankruptcy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He would reform them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He’d get that done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He hasn’t even made a proposal on either one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said in his first year he’d put out an immigration plan that would deal with our immigration challenges.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Didn’t even file it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is a president who has not been able to do what he said he’d do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said that he’d cut in half the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He hasn’t done that either.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In fact, he doubled it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said that by now middle-income families would have a reduction in their health insurance premiums by $2,500 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s gone up by $2,500 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And if Obamacare is passed, or implemented — it’s already been passed — if it’s implemented fully, it’ll be another $2,500 on top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The middle class is getting crushed under the policies of a president who has not understood what it takes to get the economy working again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He keeps saying, “Look, I’ve created 5 million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” That’s after losing 5 million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The entire record is such that the unemployment has not been reduced in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The unemployment, the number of people who are still looking for work, is still 23 million Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There are more people in poverty, one out of six people in poverty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How about food stamps?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When he took office, 32 million people were on food stamps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Today, 47 million people are on food stamps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How about the growth of the economy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s growing more slowly this year than last year, and more slowly last year than the year before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president wants to do well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the policies he’s put in place from Obamacare to Dodd-Frank to his tax policies to his regulatory policies, these policies combined have not let this economy take off and grow like it could have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You might say, “Well, you got an example of one that worked better?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” Yeah, in the Reagan recession where unemployment hit 10.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 8 percent, between that period — the end of that recession and the equivalent of time to today, Ronald Reagan’s recovery created twice as many jobs as this president’s recovery.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Five million jobs doesn’t even keep up with our population growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the only reason the unemployment rate seems a little lower today is because of all the people that have dropped out of the workforce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president has tried, but his policies haven’t worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He’s great as a — as a — as a speaker and describing his plans and his vision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s wonderful, except we have a record to look at.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that record shows he just hasn’t been able to cut the deficit, to put in place reforms for Medicare and Social Security to preserve them, to get us the rising incomes we need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Median income is down $4,300 a family and 23 million Americans out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s what this election is about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s about who can get the middle class in this country a bright and prosperous future and assure our kids the kind of hope and optimism they deserve.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is for Governor Romney?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Is it Loraina?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Lorraine?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Lorraine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Good, thanks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Lorraine?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Did I get that right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you for your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And let me step back and tell you what I would like to do with our immigration policy broadly and include an answer to your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But first of all, this is a nation of immigrants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We welcome people coming to this country as immigrants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My dad was born in Mexico of American parents; Ann’s dad was born in Wales and is a first-generation American.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We welcome legal immigrants into this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want our legal system to work better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want it to be streamlined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want it to be clearer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think you have to — shouldn’t have to hire a lawyer to figure out how to get into this country legally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I also think that we should give visas to people — green cards, rather, to people who graduate with skills that we need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: People around the world with accredited degrees in science and math get a green card stapled to their diploma, come to the U.
