transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: of A.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We should make sure our legal system works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we’re going to have to stop illegal immigration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There are 4 million people who are waiting in line to get here legally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Those who’ve come here illegally take their place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I will not grant amnesty to those who have come here illegally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What I will do is I’ll put in place an employment verification system and make sure that employers that hire people who have come here illegally are sanctioned for doing so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I won’t put in place magnets for people coming here illegally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So for instance, I would not give driver’s licenses to those that have come here illegally as the president would.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The kids of those that came here illegally, those kids, I think, should have a pathway to become a permanent resident of the United States and military service, for instance, is one way they would have that kind of pathway to become a permanent resident.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now when the president ran for office, he said that he’d put in place, in his first year, a piece of legislation — he’d file a bill in his first year that would reform our — our immigration system, protect legal immigration, stop illegal immigration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He didn’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He had a Democrat House, a Democrat Senate, super majority in both Houses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Why did he fail to even promote legislation that would have provided an answer for those that want to come legally and for those that are here illegally today?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What’s a question I think the — the president will have a chance to answer right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Good, I look forward to it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Was — Lorranna — Lorraine — we are a nation of immigrants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean we’re just a few miles away from Ellis Island.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We all understand what this country has become because talent from all around the world wants to come here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: People are willing to take risks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: People who want to build on their dreams and make sure their kids have an even bigger dreams than they have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’re also a nation of laws.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what I’ve said is we need to fix a broken immigration system and I’ve done everything that I can on my own and sought cooperation from Congress to make sure that we fix the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The first thing we did was to streamline the legal immigration system, to reduce the backlog, make it easier, simpler and cheaper for people who are waiting in line, obeying the law to make sure that they can come here and contribute to our country and that’s good for our economic growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’ll start new businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’ll make things happen to create jobs here in the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we do have to deal with our border so we put more border patrol on the — any time in history and the flow of undocumented works across the border is actually lower than it’s been in 40 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I’ve also said is if we’re going to go after folks who are here illegally, we should do it smartly and go after folks who are criminals, gang bangers, people who are hurting the community, not after students, not after folks who are here just because they’re trying to figure out how to feed their families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what we’ve done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I’ve also said is for young people who come here, brought here often times by their parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Had gone to school here, pledged allegiance to the flag.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Think of this as their country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Understand themselves as Americans in every way except having papers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we should make sure that we give them a pathway to citizenship.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what I’ve done administratively.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney just said, you know he wants to help those young people too, but during the Republican primary, he said, “I will veto the DREAM Act”, that would allow these young people to have access.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” His main strategy during the Republican primary was to say, “We’re going to encourage self-deportation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” Making life so miserable on folks that they’ll leave.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He called the Arizona law a model for the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Part of the Arizona law said that law enforcement officers could stop folks because they suspected maybe they looked like they might be undocumented workers and check their papers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know what?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If my daughter or yours looks to somebody like they’re not a citizen, I don’t want — I don’t want to empower somebody like that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So, we can fix this system in a comprehensive way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when Governor Romney says, the challenge is, “Well Obama didn’t try.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” That’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I have sat down with Democrats and Republicans at the beginning of my term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I said, let’s fix this system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Including Senators previously who had supported it on the Republican side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it’s very hard for Republican’s in Congress to support comprehensive immigration reform, if their standard bearer has said that, this is not something I’m interested in supporting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No, let — let — let me go back and speak to the points that the president made and — and — and let’s get them correct.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I did not say that the Arizona law was a model for the nation in that aspect.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I said that the E-Verify portion of the Arizona law, which is — which is the portion of the law which says that employers could be able to determine whether someone is here illegally or not illegally, that that was a model for the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, I asked the president a question I think Hispanics and immigrants all over the nation have asked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He was asked this on Univision the other day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Why, when you said you’d filed legislation in your first year didn’t you do it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And he didn’t answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He — he doesn’t answer that question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said the standard bearer wasn’t for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m glad you thought I was a standard bearer four years ago, but I wasn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Four years ago you said in your first year you would file legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In his first year, I was just getting — licking my wounds from having been beaten by John McCain, all right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was not the standard bearer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My — my view is that this president should have honored his promise to do as he said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, let me mention one other thing, and that is self-deportation says let people make their own choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What I was saying is, we’re not going to round up 12 million people, undocumented illegals, and take them out of the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Instead let people make their own choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And if they — if they find that — that they can’t get the benefits here that they want and they can’t — and they can’t find the job they want, then they’ll make a decision to go a place where — where they have better opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I’m not in favor of rounding up people and — and — and taking them out of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I am in favor, as the president has said, and I agree with him, which is that if people have committed crimes we got to get them out of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me mention something else the president said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It was a moment ago and I didn’t get a chance to, when he was describing Chinese investments and so forth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Candy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Hold on a second.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, I’m still speaking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, let me finish.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve gotta continue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Just going to make a point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Any investments I have over the last eight years have been managed by a blind trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I understand they do include investments outside the United States, including in — in Chinese companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, have you looked at your pension?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Have you looked at your pension?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got to say…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, have you looked at your pension?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, I — I don’t look at my pension.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not as big as yours so it doesn’t take as long.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me give you some advice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I don’t check it that often.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you some advice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look at your pension.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You also have investments in Chinese companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You also have investments outside the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You also have investments through a Cayman’s trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I thought we were talking about immigration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I do want to make sure that…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I do want to make sure that — I do want to make sure that we just understand something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney says he wasn’t referring to Arizona as a model for the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: His top adviser on immigration is the guy who designed the Arizona law, the entirety of it; not E-Verify, the whole thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s his policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it’s a bad policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it won’t help us grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, when we think about immigration, we have to understand there are folks all around the world who still see America as the land of promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they provide us energy and they provide us innovation and they start companies like Intel and Google.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we want to encourage that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, we’ve got to make sure that we do it in a smart way and a comprehensive way, and we make the legal system better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when we make this into a divisive political issue, and when we don’t have bipartisan support — I can deliver, Governor, a whole bunch of Democrats to get comprehensive immigration reform done, and we can’t…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First year…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … we can’t — we have not seen Republicans serious about this issue at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it’s time for them to get serious on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This used to be a bipartisan issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Hi, Kerry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What’s your name?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Great to see you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ah.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me first of all talk about our diplomats, because they serve all around the world and do an incredible job in a very dangerous situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And these aren’t just representatives of the United States, they are my representatives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I send them there, oftentimes into harm’s way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I know these folks and I know their families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So nobody is more concerned about their safety and security than I am.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So as soon as we found out that the Benghazi consulate was being overrun, I was on the phone with my national security team and I gave them three instructions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one, beef up our security and procedures, not just in Libya, but at every embassy and consulate in the region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, investigate exactly what happened, regardless of where the facts lead us, to make sure folks are held accountable and it doesn’t happen again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And number three, we are going to find out who did this and we’re going to hunt them down, because one of the things that I’ve said throughout my presidency is when folks mess with Americans, we go after them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now Governor Romney had a very different response.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: While we were still dealing with our diplomats being threatened, Governor Romney put out a press release, trying to make political points, and that’s not how a commander in chief operates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You don’t turn national security into a political issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Certainly not right when it’s happening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And people — not everybody agrees with some of the decisions I’ve made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when it comes to our national security, I mean what I say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said I’d end the war in Libya — in — in Iraq, and I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said that we’d go after al-Qaeda and bin Laden, we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I said we’d transition out of Afghanistan, and start making sure that Afghans are responsible for their own security, that’s what I’m doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to this issue, when I say that we are going to find out exactly what happened, everybody will be held accountable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I am ultimately responsible for what’s taking place there because these are my folks, and I’m the one who has to greet those coffins when they come home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know that I mean what I say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you Kerry for your question, it’s an important one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and I — I think the president just said correctly that the buck does stop at his desk and — and he takes responsibility for — for that — for the failure in providing those security resources, and — and those terrible things may well happen from time to time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I’m — I feel very deeply sympathetic for the families of those who lost loved ones.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And today there’s a memorial service for one of those that was lost in this tragedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We — we think of their families and care for them deeply.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There were other issues associated with this — with this tragedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There were many days that passed before we knew whether this was a spontaneous demonstration, or actually whether it was a terrorist attack.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And there was no demonstration involved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It was a terrorist attack and it took a long time for that to be told to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Whether there was some misleading, or instead whether we just didn’t know what happened, you have to ask yourself why didn’t we know five days later when the ambassador to the United Nations went on TV to say that this was a demonstration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How could we have not known?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I find more troubling than this, that on — on the day following the assassination of the United States ambassador, the first time that’s happened since 1979, when — when we have four Americans killed there, when apparently we didn’t know what happened, that the president, the day after that happened, flies to Las Vegas for a political fund-raiser, then the next day to Colorado for another event, other political event.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think these — these actions taken by a president and a leader have symbolic significance and perhaps even material significance in that you’d hope that during that time we could call in the people who were actually eyewitnesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve read their accounts now about what happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It was very clear this was not a demonstration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This was an attack by terrorists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And this calls into question the president’s whole policy in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look what’s happening in Syria, in Egypt, now in Libya.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Consider the distance between ourselves and — and Israel, the president said that — that he was going to put daylight between us and Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have Iran four years closer to a nuclear bomb.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Syria — Syria’s not just a tragedy of 30,000 civilians being killed by a military, but also a strategic — strategically significant player for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s policies throughout the Middle East began with an apology tour and — and — and pursue a strategy of leading from behind, and this strategy is unraveling before our very eyes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Secretary Clinton has done an extraordinary job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But she works for me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m the president and I’m always responsible, and that’s why nobody’s more interested in finding out exactly what happened than I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The day after the attack, governor, I stood in the Rose Garden and I told the American people in the world that we are going to find out exactly what happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That this was an act of terror and I also said that we’re going to hunt down those who committed this crime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And then a few days later, I was there greeting the caskets coming into Andrews Air Force Base and grieving with the families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the suggestion that anybody in my team, whether the Secretary of State, our U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ambassador, anybody on my team would play politics or mislead when we’ve lost four of our own, governor, is offensive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what I do as president, that’s not what I do as Commander in Chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I — I…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I think interesting the president just said something which — which is that on the day after the attack he went into the Rose Garden and said that this was an act of terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You said in the Rose Garden the day after the attack, it was an act of terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It was not a spontaneous demonstration, is that what you’re saying?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Please proceed governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure we get that for the record because it took the president 14 days before he called the attack in Benghazi an act of terror.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Get the transcript.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Can you say that a little louder, Candy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This — the administration — the administration indicated this was a reaction to a video and was a spontaneous reaction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It took them a long time to say this was a terrorist act by a terrorist group.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And to suggest — am I incorrect in that regard, on Sunday, the — your secretary —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Candy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The ambassador of the United Nations went on the Sunday television shows and spoke about how —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Candy, I’m —

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: — this was a spontaneous —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m happy to have a longer conversation —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: — about foreign policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m happy to do that, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I just want to make sure that —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: — all of these wonderful folks are going to have a chance to get some of their questions answered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re a nation that believes in the Second Amendment, and I believe in the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a long tradition of hunting and sportsmen and people who want to make sure they can protect themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there have been too many instances during the course of my presidency, where I’ve had to comfort families who have lost somebody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Most recently out in Aurora.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, just a couple of weeks ago, actually, probably about a month, I saw a mother, who I had met at the bedside of her son, who had been shot in that theater.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And her son had been shot through the head.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we spent some time, and we said a prayer and, remarkably, about two months later, this young man and his mom showed up, and he looked unbelievable, good as new.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there were a lot of families who didn’t have that good fortune and whose sons or daughters or husbands didn’t survive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So my belief is that, , we have to enforce the laws we’ve already got, make sure that we’re keeping guns out of the hands of criminals, those who are mentally ill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve done a much better job in terms of background checks, but we’ve got more to do when it comes to enforcement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also share your belief that weapons that were designed for soldiers in war theaters don’t belong on our streets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so what I’m trying to do is to get a broader conversation about how do we reduce the violence generally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Part of it is seeing if we can get an assault weapons ban reintroduced.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But part of it is also looking at other sources of the violence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because frankly, in my home town of Chicago, there’s an awful lot of violence and they’re not using AK-47s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’re using cheap hand guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so what can we do to intervene, to make sure that young people have opportunity; that our schools are working; that if there’s violence on the streets, that working with faith groups and law enforcement, we can catch it before it gets out of control.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so what I want is a — is a comprehensive strategy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Part of it is seeing if we can get automatic weapons that kill folks in amazing numbers out of the hands of criminals and the mentally ill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But part of it is also going deeper and seeing if we can get into these communities and making sure we catch violent impulses before they occur.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, I’m not in favor of new pieces of legislation on — on guns and taking guns away or making certain guns illegal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We, of course, don’t want to have automatic weapons, and that’s already illegal in this country to have automatic weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What I believe is we have to do, as the president mentioned towards the end of his remarks there, which is to make enormous efforts to enforce the gun laws that we have, and to change the culture of violence that we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And you ask how — how are we going to do that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And there are a number of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He mentioned good schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I totally agree.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We were able to drive our schools to be number one in the nation in my state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I believe if we do a better job in education, we’ll — we’ll give people the — the hope and opportunity they deserve and perhaps less violence from that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But let me mention another thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that is parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need moms and dads, helping to raise kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Wherever possible the — the benefit of having two parents in the home, and that’s not always possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A lot of great single moms, single dads.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But gosh to tell our kids that before they have babies, they ought to think about getting married to someone, that’s a great idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because if there’s a two parent family, the prospect of living in poverty goes down dramatically.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The opportunities that the child will — will be able to achieve increase dramatically.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So we can make changes in the way our culture works to help bring people away from violence and give them opportunity, and bring them in the American system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The — the greatest failure we’ve had with regards to — to gun violence in some respects is what — what is known as Fast and Furious.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Which was a program under this administration, and how it worked exactly I think we don’t know precisely, where thousands of automatic, and AK-47 type weapons were — were given to people that ultimately gave them to — to drug lords.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They used those weapons against — against their own citizens and killed Americans with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And this was a — this was a program of the government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: For what purpose it was put in place, I can’t imagine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But it’s one of the great tragedies related to violence in our society which has occurred during this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Which I think the American people would like to understand fully, it’s been investigated to a degree, but — but the administration has carried out executive privilege to prevent all of the information from coming out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to understand who it was that did this, what the idea was behind it, why it led to the violence, thousands of guns going to Mexican drug lords.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: OBAMA: Candy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, Candy, actually, in my state, the pro-gun folks and the anti-gun folks came together and put together a piece of legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And it’s referred to as an assault weapon ban, but it had, at the signing of the bill, both the pro-gun and the anti-gun people came together, because it provided opportunities for both that both wanted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There were hunting opportunities, for instance, that haven’t previously been available and so forth, so it was a mutually agreed- upon piece of legislation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we need more of, Candy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What we have right now in Washington is a place that’s gridlocked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have —

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Candy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: — we haven’t had the leadership in Washington to work on a bipartisan basis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was able to do that in my state and bring these two together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The — first of all, I think Governor Romney was for an assault weapons ban before he was against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And he said that the reason he changed his mind was, in part, because he was seeking the endorsement of the National Rifle Association.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So that’s on the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I think that one area we agree on is the important of parents and the importance of schools, because I do believe that if our young people have opportunity, then they are less likely to engage in these kinds of violent acts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to eliminate everybody who is mentally disturbed and we have got to make sure they don’t get weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we can make a difference in terms ensuring that every young person in America, regardless of where they come from, what they look like, have a chance to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, Candy, we haven’t had a chance to talk about education much, but I think it is very important to understand that the reforms we’ve put in place, working with 46 governors around the country, are seeing schools that are some of the ones that are the toughest for kids starting to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re starting to see gains in math and science.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to community colleges, we are setting up programs, including with Nassau Community College, to retrain workers, including young people who may have dropped out of school but now are getting another chance, training them for the jobs that exist right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And in fact, employers are looking for skilled workers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so we’re matching them up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Giving them access to higher education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: As I said, we have made sure that millions of young people are able to get an education that they weren’t able to get before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But — but it’ll — it’ll — it’ll be…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … just one second.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because — because this is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is part of the choice in this election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When Governor Romney was asked whether teachers, hiring more teachers was important to growing our economy, Governor Romney said that doesn’t grow our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When — when he was asked would class size…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But this will make a difference in terms of whether or not we can move this economy forward for these young people…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … and reduce our violence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Boy, great question and important question, because you’re absolutely right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The place where we’ve seen manufacturing go has been China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: China is now the largest manufacturer in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It used to be the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A lot of good people have lost jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A half a million manufacturing jobs have been lost in the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s total over the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons for that is that people think it’s more attractive in some cases to go offshore than to stay here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have made it less attractive for enterprises to stay here than to go offshore from time to time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What I will do as president is make sure it’s more attractive to come to America again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is the way we’re going to create jobs in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not by trickle-down government, saying we’re going to take more money from people and hire more government workers, raise more taxes, put in place more regulations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Trickle-down government has never worked here, has never worked anywhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to make America the most attractive place in the world for entrepreneurs, for small business, for big business, to invest and grow in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, we’re going to have to make sure that as we trade with other nations that they play by the rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And China hasn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons — or one of the ways they don’t play by the rules is artificially holding down the value of their currency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Because if they put their currency down low, that means their prices on their goods are low.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that makes them advantageous in the marketplace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We lose sales.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And manufacturers here in the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: making the same products can’t compete.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: China has been a currency manipulator for years and years and years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the president has a regular opportunity to label them as a currency manipulator, but refuses to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: On day one, I will label China a currency manipulator, which will allow me as president to be able to put in place, if necessary, tariffs where I believe that they are taking unfair advantage of our manufacturers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So we’re going to make sure that people we trade with around the world play by the rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But let me — let me not just stop there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Don’t forget, what’s key to bringing back jobs here is not just finding someone else to punish, and I’m going to be strict with people who we trade with to make sure they — they follow the law and play by the rules, but it’s also to make America the most attractive place in the world for businesses of all kinds.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I want to down the tax rates on small employers, big employers, so they want to be here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Canada’s tax rate on companies is now 15 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Ours is 35 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So if you’re starting a business, where would you rather start it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to be competitive if we’re going to create more jobs here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Regulations have quadrupled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The rate of regulations quadrupled under this president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I talk to small businesses across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They say, “We feel like we’re under attack from our own government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” I want to make sure that regulators see their job as encouraging small business, not crushing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And there’s no question but that Obamacare has been an extraordinary deterrent to enterprises of all kinds hiring people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My priority is making sure that we get more people hired.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If we have more people hired, if we get back manufacturing jobs, if we get back all kinds of jobs into this country, then you’re going to see rising incomes again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The reason incomes are down is because unemployment is so high.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know what it takes to get this to happen, and my plan will do that, and one part of it is to make sure that we keep China playing by the rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need to create jobs here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And both Governor Romney and I agree actually that we should lower our corporate tax rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s too high.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there’s a difference in terms of how we would do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to close loopholes that allow companies to deduct expenses when they move to China; that allow them to profit offshore and not have to get taxed, so they have tax advantages offshore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: All those changes in our tax code would make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney actually wants to expand those tax breaks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: One of his big ideas when it comes to corporate tax reform would be to say, if you invest overseas, you make profits overseas, you don’t have to pay U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, of course, if you’re a small business or a mom-and-pop business or a big business starting up here, you’ve got to pay even the reduced rate that Governor Romney’s talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it’s estimated that that will create 800,000 new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The problem is they’ll be in china.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Or India.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Or Germany.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the way we’re going to create jobs here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The way we’re going to create jobs here is not just to change our tax code, but also to double our exports.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are on pace to double our exports, one of the commitments I made when I was president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s creating tens of thousands of jobs all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we’ve kept on pushing trade deals, but trade deals that make sure that American workers and American businesses are getting a good deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney talked about China, as I already indicated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the private sector, Governor Romney’s company invested in what were called pioneers of outsourcing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not my phrase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what reporters called it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as far as currency manipulation, the currency has actually gone up 11 percent since I’ve been president because we have pushed them hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve put unprecedented trade pressure on China.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why exports have significantly increased under my presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s going to help to create jobs here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The answer is very straightforward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We can compete with anyone in the world as long as the playing field is level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: China’s been cheating over the years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One by holding down the value of their currency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, by stealing our intellectual property; our designs, our patents, our technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There’s even an Apple store in China that’s a counterfeit Apple store, selling counterfeit goods.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They hack into our computers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We will have to have people play on a fair basis, that’s number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, we have to make America the most attractive place for entrepreneurs, for people who want to expand their business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s what brings jobs in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s characterization of my tax plan…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …is completely…is completely…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: …is completely false.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Candy, there are some jobs that are not going to come back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because they are low wage, low skill jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want high wage, high skill jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we have to emphasize manufacturing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we have to invest in advanced manufacturing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we’ve got to make sure that we’ve got the best science and research in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when we talk about deficits, if we’re adding to our deficit for tax cuts for folks who don’t need them, and we’re cutting investments in research and science that will create the next Apple, create the next new innovation that will sell products around the world, we will lose that race.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we’re not training engineers to make sure that they are equipped here in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Then companies won’t come here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Those investments are what’s going to help to make sure that we continue to lead this world economy, not just next year, but 10 years from now, 50 years from now, 100 years from now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Government does not create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Government does not create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Barry?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Where is Barry?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, and that’s an opportunity for me, and I appreciate it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In the nature of a campaign, it seems that some campaigns are focused on attacking a person rather than prescribing their own future and the things they’d like to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In the course of that, I think the president’s campaign has tried to characterize me as — as someone who’s very different than who I am.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I care about 100 percent of the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want 100 percent of the American people to have a bright and prosperous future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I care about our kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I understand what it takes to make a bright and prosperous future for America again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I spent my life in the private sector, not in government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m a guy who wants to help with the experience I have, the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My — my passion probably flows from the fact that I believe in God.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I believe we’re all children of the same God.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I believe we have a responsibility to care for one another.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I served as a missionary for my church.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I served as a pastor in my congregation for about 10 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve sat across the table from people who were out of work and worked with them to try and find new work or to help them through tough times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I went to the Olympics when they were in trouble to try and get them on track.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And as governor of my state, I was able to get 100 percent of my people insured, all my kids, about 98 percent of the adults.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was able also to get our schools ranked number one in the nation, so 100 percent of our kids would have a bright opportunity for a future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I understand that I can get this country on track again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to settle for what we’re going through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to settle for gasoline at four bucks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to settle for unemployment at a chronically high level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to settle for 47 million people on food stamps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to settle for 50 percent of kids coming out of college not able to get work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have to settle for 23 million people struggling to find a good job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If I become president, I’ll get America working again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will get us on track to a balanced budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president hasn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll make sure we can reform Medicare and Social Security to preserve them for coming — coming generations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president said he would.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get our incomes up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, I’ve done these things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I served as governor and showed I could get them done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Barry, I think a lot of this campaign, maybe over the last four years, has been devoted to this nation that I think government creates jobs, that that somehow is the answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what I believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I believe that the free enterprise system is the greatest engine of prosperity the world’s ever known.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I believe in self-reliance and individual initiative and risk takers being rewarded.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe that everybody should have a fair shot and everybody should do their fair share and everybody should play by the same rules, because that’s how our economy’s grown.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we built the world’s greatest middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And — and that is part of what’s at stake in this election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s a fundamentally different vision about how we move our country forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I believe Governor Romney is a good man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Loves his family, cares about his faith.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe that when he said behind closed doors that 47 percent of the country considered themselves victims who refuse personal responsibility, think about who he was talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Folks on Social Security who’ve worked all their lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Veterans who’ve sacrificed for this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Students who are out there trying to hopefully advance their own dreams, but also this country’s dreams.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Soldiers who are overseas fighting for us right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: People who are working hard every day, paying payroll tax, gas taxes, but don’t make enough income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I want to fight for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I’ve been doing for the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because if they succeed, I believe the country succeeds.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When my grandfather fought in World War II and he came back and he got a G.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bill and that allowed him to go to college, that wasn’t a handout.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That was something that advanced the entire country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
